# Helping Your Midwife Find You

*A page from the Riverside Community Midwives welcome pack*

## Hello, we are coming as friends

Where I come from, the midwife is like family. That is how we feel too. When your baby is coming, we are not just turning up for work. We are coming to be with you.

But there is one small problem. **We are very good at catching babies and not always so good at finding your house.** I am the worst on our team, and that is why I got to write this page.

Read it once, tick the list at the end, and stick it on your fridge. Then at 3am, nobody has to think.

## First, when does home birth cover start?

**From 37 weeks.** Before 37 weeks, please go to the hospital.

We tell everyone at the booking visit, but it is a lot to remember, so here it is again. Maybe write "37 weeks" on the calendar.

## Step 1: Call the Riverside birth line

When labour starts, phone the **Riverside birth line**:

📞 **[ADD BIRTH LINE NUMBER HERE]**

Please do **not** call your midwife's personal mobile. Yes, even if you have it. The birth line goes to whoever is on call, so someone will always pick up. Your usual midwife might be asleep, on holiday, or stuck behind a bus.

When you call, have these ready:

- Your full address and postcode
- Which entrance, floor or building you are in, if you live in a flat
- A phone number we can call back

If you are worried at any time, or it is an emergency, call **999**.

## Step 2: Help us find your door

This is the most important part. Sat navs are clever, but they are not always right. Here are some true stories.

**The flats in Everton.** I once drove round and round a block of flats for 20 minutes. Flat 14 was not next to flat 13. It was in a different building! In the end, the dad was waving a tea towel from the window. It worked. I will never forget it.

**The house with no number.** Some houses only have a name, like "Rosemary Cottage", in a long street of terraces. My sat nav took me to a chippy. Lovely chips, wrong baby.

**The wrong house.** One time, I walked into the wrong house because the door was open. A very nice old man gave me a Jammie Dodger anyway. I did not find the baby, but I did get a biscuit.

So, here is how to help us:

- **Put the porch light on at night, please!** In winter, dark streets all look the same.
- **Put balloons on your gate or door.** One family did this like it was a birthday party. It was the best idea ever. I found them straight away. Any colour is fine. Make it silly.
- **Make your house number big and clear.** If your house only has a name, put the number on a piece of paper in the window.
- **Send us a pin.** Share your **what3words** address, or send a location pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. (It is a good tool, I was surprised.)
- **Flats:** Tell us the building, the entrance, the floor, and any door code. Is there a lift? Does the buzzer work?
- **Send someone to wait outside.** A partner, a friend, or a big sister. Waving is welcome. Tea towels are optional but proven.

Please keep the door closed until we arrive. Someone will let us in. We will knock, and we promise we will not walk into the neighbours.

## Step 3: Parking

Two midwives come to a home birth, and we usually arrive in **two separate cars**. So, if you can, please keep **two parking spaces** free near your door.

If you live in a permit zone, like around **Anfield and Kensington**, please:

- Ask the council about a **visitor permit** before the baby comes, or
- Have one **ready to put on the dashboard**

We have had parking tickets before. Nobody wants to be told off by a traffic warden at 4am while holding a gas cylinder.

## Step 4: Inside the house

We carry a lot. Gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes the birthing pool things. By the time we reach your door, our arms are very tired. A clear path makes a big difference.

Please:

- **Clear the stairs and the hallway.** No shoes, no washing basket, no Lego. (Lego hurts. Ask any parent.)
- **Put pets in another room.** I love dogs, really. One friendly staffie loved me so much that he jumped on me every visit, and I nearly dropped the Entonox. Please keep your pets in another room, with a door closed, when baby is coming. They will be fine, and they can meet the baby later.
- **Keep the path to the birthing room clear,** and leave a bit of space around the door.

Do not worry about a messy house. We are not here to look at the dust. We just do not want anyone to trip.

## Your fridge checklist

Tick these off before you reach 37 weeks. Stick this on the fridge.

☐ I know home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**. Before that, I go to the hospital.

☐ The **Riverside birth line number** is saved in my phone and on the fridge. I will **not** call my midwife's personal mobile.

☐ I know my **what3words** address, or I know how to send a **WhatsApp pin**.

☐ My **house number** is big and easy to see, or I have a sign ready for the window.

☐ **Flat dwellers:** I know our building, entrance, floor and door code, and I will tell the midwives.

☐ The **porch light** will go on when labour starts.

☐ **Balloons** are ready for the gate or door. (Optional, but I would not skip them.)

☐ Someone knows their job is to **wait outside** and wave us in.

☐ I have asked about a **visitor permit** if I live in a permit zone, or one is ready for the dashboard.

☐ There is space for **two cars** near the door, if possible.

☐ The **stairs and hallway are clear**: no shoes, no washing basket, no Lego.

☐ I know where the **pets** will go, and the door will be closed.

## See you soon

When labour starts, take a breath and call the birth line. Put the light on, tie the balloons, and put the kettle on. We will find you.

And if we get a bit lost, please wave a tea towel.

*Riverside Community Midwives*

---

A few notes for you:

- I left a gap for the **birth line number**. Please add it before this goes in the folder or on Facebook.
- I added the **999 line** for emergencies. It is standard, but check with Deb that it fits your team's guidance.
- I did not name Pippin, the Rosemary Cottage street, or the Everton flats, because the page goes on a Facebook group where families might recognise themselves. Easy to change if you prefer.
- I did not add any rules about *when* to call in labour, because that was not in your notes. If your team has a standard line, it would fit nicely at the top of Step 1.
